Barren

/BARE-en/ — rhymes with Karen · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Land that is barren is so dry, empty, or infertile that little or nothing can grow there.

Nothing grew on the barren hillside except a few tufts of dry grass.

Worked Example

The desert explorer trudged across the barren expanse where the parched earth cracked beneath her feet and nothing could survive.

Barren precisely captures why the land is empty—it's unable to support life due to being both dry and infertile. Just saying 'empty' wouldn't explain the reason; 'barren' shows both the dryness and the lifelessness.

How Barren Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

empty

empty: containing nothing at all inside it

arid

arid: extremely dry, with almost no rain

desolate

desolate: bleak, deserted, and empty of life

Antonyms

fertile

fertile: rich land where plants grow easily

lush

lush: thick with green, healthy plant growth

How Strong Is It? — bare → fertile → lush → barren

bare vs. barren

bare vs. barren: Bare is milder than barren: a bare field is simply empty right now, while a barren field cannot produce life at all.

fertile vs. barren

fertile vs. barren: Fertile is barren's opposite, sitting at the abundant end of the scale: fertile land bursts with new growth — the very thing barren land cannot do.

lush vs. barren

lush vs. barren: Lush is the farthest extreme from barren, even richer than fertile: lush land is so thick with green, healthy growth that it is the total reverse of a barren landscape.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — baraigne

Root — baraigne: sterile; unable to produce offspring or crops (Anglo-Norman / Old French)

Put it together

Put it together: Barren keeps almost exactly its Old French meaning: baraigne described animals, plants, or land that could not produce offspring or crops. Barren land today is the same — so dry, empty, or infertile that little or nothing can grow there.

Use the root in a new word: barrenness

Use the root in a new word: barrenness: Explorers wrote about the barrenness of the high desert — mile after mile of barren rock where nothing grew; barrenness is the noun built straight from barren.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Barren is specific to land or soil that cannot grow things because it is too dry and infertile. Empty just means the space has no contents. Barren emphasizes the inability to produce life.
